Quiet Infrastructure

By Lee Park

Engineers measured the current twice, then a third time, hoping the instruments were wrong. When the first shipment arrived, nobody cheered, but several people stayed late to unpack it. The report concluded that patience, not funding, had been the scarce resource all along.

Critics called the plan sentimental; the accountants called it the cheapest option on the table. A small cooperative formed, fragile at first, then stubborn, then quietly indispensable. When the first shipment arrived, nobody cheered, but several people stayed late to unpack it.
